Write the OSF preregistration text that a spec determines

Source: R/tteplan_osf_text.R
tteplan_osf_text.Rd

Writes the text of each field of the OSF Preregistration form whose content the study specification and swereg fix: the design, the sampling, the treatment strategies, the outcomes, the covariates, the eligibility criteria, the analysis, the minimum-events rule and the code list. Each fact appears in one field. The other fields point to it as 'Field/Subheading'.

Usage

tteplan_osf_text(
  spec_path,
  code_registry = NULL,
  period_width = 4L,
  global_max_isoyearweek = NULL,
  people = c("person", "persons")
)

Arguments

spec_path

Character(1), the path of the spec YAML. The function reads it with tteplan_read_spec().

code_registry

The code registry that resolves each variable to its codes, as in tteplan_excel_spec_summary(): NULL, a RegistryStudy, or a data.table with the columns of RegistryStudy$summary_table(). With NULL, every code cell of the code list reads not resolved.

period_width

Integer, the width in weeks of the enrollment period. It has the default of tteplan_from_spec_and_registrystudy().

global_max_isoyearweek

Character(1) or NULL, the administrative censoring boundary as an isoyearweek, for example "2025-01". Follow-up includes that week. NULL writes "the administrative end of the data".

people

Character(2), the singular and plural noun for a study participant, for example c("woman", "women").

Value

A named character vector. Each element is the Markdown text of one field, and the names are the OSF field headings: Study design, Sample size, Measured variables/Exposures, Measured variables/Outcomes, Measured variables/Baseline covariates, Statistical models, Transformations, Inference criteria, Data inclusion and exclusion, Missing data, Other planned analysis and Code list. Inference criteria states the minimum-events rule from min_expected_events_per_arm_per_year.

Details

The function reads the spec and the code registry only. It reads no skeleton, rawbatch or registry data file, so it runs before s0. Every spec entry appears in the text: no criterion, covariate or outcome is left out.

The text uses the name of each criterion, covariate and outcome, the arms and description of each treatment, and the description of each outcome, as the spec writes them. Write those fields for a reader of the registration. An age range and an ISO-year range are written from their min and max, the values that run, and not from their name. The categories of each covariate are data values, so they appear in the code list only.

Fields that the spec cannot answer are left to the author: the title, the research question and the primary result, the foreknowledge of the data, the data sources and the study population, and the ethics approval.

See also

tteplan_excel_spec_summary(), vignette("tte-methods")

Other tte_spec: tteplan_apply_derived_confounders(), tteplan_apply_exclusions(), tteplan_excel_spec_summary(), tteplan_from_spec_and_registrystudy(), tteplan_read_spec(), tteplan_validate_spec()

Examples

spec_dir <- tempfile()
dir.create(spec_dir)
spec_path <- file.path(spec_dir, "spec_v001.yaml")
writeLines(
  c(
    "study:",
    "  title: Example study",
    "  implementation:",
    "    project_prefix: example",
    "    version: v001",
    "inclusion_criteria:",
    "  isoyears: [2010, 2020]",
    "exclusion_criteria:",
    "  - name: Prior oophorectomy",
    "    implementation:",
    "      source_variable: os_oophorectomy",
    "      window: lifetime_before_baseline",
    "confounders:",
    "  - name: Age",
    "    implementation:",
    "      variable: rd_age_continuous",
    "outcomes:",
    "  - name: Outcome",
    "    implementation:",
    "      variable: osd_outcome",
    "follow_up:",
    "  - {label: 1 year, weeks: 52}",
    "min_expected_events_per_arm_per_year: 5",
    "enrollments:",
    "  - id: '01'",
    "    name: A vs B",
    "    observed_var: {sentinel: row_presence}",
    "    intervention_tolerance_weeks: 0",
    "    comparator_tolerance_weeks: 0",
    "    additional_inclusion:",
    "      - {name: Age 50-59, type: age_range, min: 50, max: 59}",
    "    treatment:",
    "      arms: {intervention: A, comparator: B}",
    "      implementation:",
    "        variable: rd_tx",
    "        intervention_value: a",
    "        comparator_value: b",
    "        comparator_to_intervention_ratio: 2",
    "        seed: 1"
  ),
  spec_path
)
osf <- tteplan_osf_text(spec_path)
cat(osf[["Data inclusion and exclusion"]])
#> Each criterion is assessed in each week of the enrollment period. A look-back window counts the calendar weeks before the week assessed, not that week itself. 'At any time before baseline' means from the start of the data.
#> 
#> Inclusion criteria:
#> 
#> 1. Trial entry in ISO years 2010 to 2020.
#> 2. Age 50 to 59 years.
#> 
#> Exclusion criteria:
#> 
#> 1. Prior oophorectomy, at any time before baseline.
#> 
#> No person is excluded for an extreme value of a measured variable. Extreme weights are truncated, as described under 'Statistical models'.
unlink(spec_dir, recursive = TRUE)
